metadata.title: Claude, Debug Zoom Integration.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude jumps straight to a fix when a Zoom integration breaks, or does something else first, using the skill's real mechanism (isolate the failing layer among auth/webhooks/SDK-join/MCP-transport/media before proposing anything) with an invented 'join button spins' scenario as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that isolation happens before any fix, in a fixed order.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B03 (five-layer stack planted with the invented 'join button spins' scenario; paid off with the isolate-then-confirm sequence landing on MCP Transport, plus the outside-scope branch)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes that when a Zoom integration breaks, Claude just jumps in and fixes it right away. It doesn't. The real question: does Claude isolate which layer failed before it touches any code?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A Zoom join breaks — does Claude just fix it right away?', hesitates on 'fix', corrects to 'isolate', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('fix' -> 'isolate') is visible on a late frame.

beats.act: 1 stakes / 2 wrong guess, falsified / 4 ANCHOR PLANTED
beats.narration_text: Take a Zoom integration where the join button spins and never connects. Before Claude touches anything, it reads debug-zoom-integration — a SKILL.md file naming five places the failure could be: authentication, webhooks, the SDK join call, MCP transport, or the real-time media stream itself.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — five layer cards draw in left to right; none lit; the 'join button spins, never connects' scenario types in beneath

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — five layers, none checked yet
production_viz.mechanic: Five small cards labelled Auth / Webhooks / SDK Join / MCP Transport / Media draw in left to right on cream, flat grey outlines, none lit. THE ANCHOR. Beneath the row, a short italic line types itself out: "join button spins — never connects." A caption beneath reads 'nothing isolated yet.' No fix icon anywhere in frame. THIS EXACT FIVE-CARD ROW RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The skill's steps run in a fixed order: check one layer, confirm it's clean, move to the next — never skip ahead, never guess which layer to check first.

shot.new_visual_element: The five-card row; a check mark lands on each card in turn, left to right, one at a time

production_viz.label: One layer at a time, in order
production_viz.mechanic: The same five-card row from B01 redraws. A teal check mark lands on Auth, then a beat later on Webhooks, then SDK Join — each check appearing only after the previous one has landed, never two at once. MCP Transport and Media stay flat and unchecked, waiting their turn. Caption beneath: 'no skipping ahead.'

beats.narration_text: Auth checks out. Webhooks check out. SDK join checks out. The break is in MCP transport — and only now, with the layer confirmed, does the skill propose a fix. Ask it about something outside those five layers, and it has nothing to add; the same steps just don't run.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — checks land on auth/webhooks/SDK-join; MCP Transport gets the one accent mark and the fix note; a sixth 'outside the five' card stays blank

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — confirmed, then fixed
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01/B02 FIVE-CARD ROW RETURNS, identical layout. Teal checks land on Auth, Webhooks, SDK Join in sequence. On MCP Transport, a single terracotta ring lands instead of a check — the confirmed break, the first and only accent mark anywhere in this beat — and only then does a small 'fix proposed' note fade in beside it. Media stays untouched; it was never reached. Beneath the row, a sixth faint card reading 'outside the five?' appears with no marks at all and a caption: 'nothing to add.'

beats.narration_text: Before Claude proposes a fix, it isolates which layer actually broke — same order, every time, and nothing outside that list.

props.quote: Before Claude proposes a fix, it isolates which layer actually broke — same order, every time, and nothing outside that list.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Before you propose any fix for this bug, walk me through every layer that could be responsible, and check them one at a time, out loud, in order — don't jump to a patch until you've isolated which one actually broke. Paste it onto a bug you're stuck on right now, then watch whether Claude actually isolates first, or guesses. Liam, in for Bear.
